modern: His walk may be slow, but it is sure. He who hurries to get rich won’t be innocent or safe; but steady perseverance in integrity, even if it doesn’t bring riches, will certainly bring peace. In doing what is just and right we are like someone walking on a rock, for we are confident that every step we take is on solid, safe ground. On the other hand, the greatest success gained through shady dealings must always be hollow and treacherous, and the man who has gained it must always be afraid that a day of reckoning will come, and then his gains will condemn him.

Let’s stick to truth and righteousness. By God’s grace let’s imitate our Lord and Master, in whose mouth no deceit was ever found. Let’s not be afraid of being poor, or of being treated with contempt. Never, on any account at all, let’s do what our conscience can’t justify. If we lose inner peace, we lose more than a fortune can buy. If we keep to the Lord’s own way and never sin against our conscience, our way is safe against all comers. Who can harm us if we are followers of what is good? We may be thought fools by fools if we stand firm in our integrity; but in the place where judgment never errs, we will be approved.

notes.term: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely
notes.note: “But he that perverteth his ways shall be known” ([[Prov.10.9|Proverbs 10:9]]).

notes.term: He that hasteth to be rich
notes.note: “He that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent” ([[Prov.28.20|Proverbs 28:20]]); “He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye” ([[Prov.28.22|Proverbs 28:22]]).

notes.term: In whose mouth no deceit was ever found
notes.note: “Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth” ([[1Pet.2.22|1 Peter 2:22]]).

notes.term: Who is he that can harm us
notes.note: “And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?” ([[1Pet.3.13|1 Peter 3:13]]).
Never wrong.

modern: This is the way to live. With God always before us, we’ll have the noblest company, the holiest example, the sweetest comfort and the mightiest influence. This must be a deliberate act of the mind: “I have set,” and it must be kept up as a set and settled thing. Always to keep an eye on the Lord’s eye, and an ear for the Lord’s voice: this is the right state for the godly person. His God is near him, filling the horizon of his vision, leading the way of his life and supplying the theme of his meditation. What vanities we would avoid, what sins we would overcome, what virtues we would show, what joys we would experience, if we really did set the Lord always before us! Why not?

This is the way to be safe. With the Lord always in our minds, we come to feel safe and sure because he is so near. He is at our right hand to guide and help us, and so we aren’t moved by fear or force or fraud or fickleness. When God stands at a man’s right hand, that man is sure to stand. Come on, then, you enemies of the truth! Rush at me like a furious storm, if you like. God holds me up. God stays with me. Whom shall I fear?

notes.term: I have set the Lord always before me
notes.note: [[Ps.16.8|Psalm 16:8]], which Peter applies to Christ ([[Acts.2.25|Acts 2:25]]).
Comfort.
Supplying.
Emptiness, worthlessness: anything that promises much and gives nothing. Not only pride in your looks.
Enemies.
“The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?” ([[Ps.27.1|Psalm 27:1]]).

modern: It is the height of grace that Jehovah should be in covenant with man, a feeble, sinful and dying creature. Yet the Lord has solemnly entered into a faithful agreement with us, and he will never turn aside from that covenant. Because of this covenant we are safe. As lions and wolves are driven off by shepherds, so all harmful influences will be chased away. The Lord will give us rest from those who disturb and destroy; the evil beasts will be gone from the land. O Lord, make this promise of yours good even now!

The Lord’s people are to enjoy security in the most exposed places: wildernesses and woods are to be like pastures and folds to Christ’s flock. If the Lord doesn’t change the place for the better, he will make us better in the place. The wilderness isn’t a place to live in, but the Lord can make it one; in the woods you feel you must keep watch rather than sleep, and yet the Lord gives his beloved sleep even there. Nothing outside or inside should make the child of God afraid. By faith the wilderness can become the suburbs of heaven, and the woods the entrance hall of glory.

notes.term: I will make them a covenant of peace
notes.note: [[Ezek.34.25|Ezekiel 34:25]], from God’s promise to be his people’s shepherd.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
A binding agreement.
Because of.
Harmful.

notes.term: The Lord giveth His beloved sleep
notes.note: “For so he giveth his beloved sleep” ([[Ps.127.2|Psalm 127:2]]).
An entrance hall.

modern: A condescending picture indeed! Just as a hen protects her brood and lets them nestle under her wings, so the Lord will defend his people and let them hide in him. Haven’t we seen the little chicks peeping out from under their mother’s feathers? Haven’t we heard their little cry of contented joy? Let’s shelter in our God like that, and feel overflowing peace in knowing that he is guarding us.
While the Lord covers us, we trust. It would be strange if we didn’t. How can we distrust when Jehovah himself becomes house and home, refuge and rest to us?

With this done, we go out to war in his name and enjoy the same guardian care. We need shield and buckler, and when we trust God completely, just as the chick trusts the hen, we find his truth arming us from head to foot. The Lord can’t lie; he must be faithful to his people; his promise must stand. This sure truth is all the shield we need. Behind it we defy the fiery darts of the enemy.
Come, my soul, hide under those great wings; lose yourself among those soft feathers! How happy you are!

notes.term: He shall cover thee with his feathers

notes.note: Stooping down from a high position, in the good sense, without today’s sense of looking down on someone. A simile is a comparison.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
A small round shield.
Completely, without question.
“God, that cannot lie” ([[Titus.1.2|Titus 1:2]]).

notes.term: The fiery darts of the enemy
notes.note: “The shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked” ([[Eph.6.16|Ephesians 6:16]]).

modern: The man God has given grace to live a blameless life lives in perfect security.

He lives on high, above the world, out of the enemy’s gunshot and near to heaven. He has high aims and motives, and he finds high comforts and company. He rejoices in the mountains of eternal love, where he has his home.
He is defended by fortresses of towering rock. The firmest things in the universe are the promises and purposes of the unchanging God, and these are the safeguard of the obedient believer.

He is provided for by this great promise: “Bread shall be given him.” As the enemy can’t climb the fort or break down the rampart, so the fortress can’t be taken by siege and famine. The Lord, who rained manna in the wilderness, will keep his people well supplied even when they are surrounded by those who would starve them.

But what if the water fails? That can’t happen: “his waters shall be sure.” There is a never-failing well inside the impregnable fortress. The Lord sees to it that nothing is lacking. No one can touch the citizen of the true Zion. However fierce the enemy, the Lord will preserve his chosen.

notes.note: Promised to “he that walketh righteously” ([[Isa.33.15-Isa.33.16|Isaiah 33:15–16]]).
Fortifications.
Enormous, astonishing.
“Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you” ([[Exod.16.4|Exodus 16:4]]).
Well supplied.
Impossible to capture.
Lacking.
The city of God; here, God’s people and their home in heaven ([[Heb.12.22|Hebrews 12:22]]).

modern: There is no bridge: we must go through the waters and feel the rush of the rivers. God’s presence in the flood is better than a ferryboat. Tested we must be, but triumphant we will be; for Jehovah himself, who is mightier than many waters, will be with us. Whenever else he may be away from his people, the Lord will surely be with them in difficulties and dangers. The sorrows of life may rise to an extraordinary height, but the Lord is equal to every occasion.

The enemies of God can put dangers of their own making in our way, such as persecutions and cruel mockings, which are like a burning fiery furnace. What then? We’ll walk through the fires. With God with us, we won’t be burned; no, not even the smell of fire will stay on us.

Oh, the wonderful security of the pilgrim born of heaven and bound for heaven! Floods can’t drown him, and fires can’t burn him. Your presence, O Lord, protects your saints from the many dangers of the road. Look, in faith I commit myself to you, and my spirit enters into rest.

notes.term: When thou passest through the waters

notes.note: The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
“The LORD on high is mightier than the noise of many waters” ([[Ps.93.4|Psalm 93:4]]).

notes.term: A burning fiery furnace… not even the smell of fire
notes.note: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego came out of Nebuchadnezzar’s furnace unharmed: “nor the smell of fire had passed on them” ([[Dan.3.27|Daniel 3:27]]).
No.

modern: David had just heard the voice of the Lord in a thunderstorm and seen his power in the hurricane whose path he described; and now, in the cool calm after the storm, that overwhelming power that shakes heaven and earth is promised as the strength of the chosen. He who sends the lightning bolt straight to its mark will give his redeemed the wings of eagles. He who shakes the earth with his voice will terrify the enemies of his saints and give his children peace. Why are we weak when we have God’s strength to run to? Why are we troubled when the Lord’s own peace is ours? Jesus, the mighty God, is our strength; let’s put him on and go out to our service. Jesus, our blessed Lord, is also our peace; let’s rest in him today and put an end to our fears. What a blessing to have him as our strength and our peace, both now and forever!

The same God who rides on the storm in days of tempest will also rule the hurricane of our trouble, and before long send us days of peace. We’ll have strength for storms and songs for fair weather. Let’s start singing at once to God our strength and our peace. Away, dark thoughts! Up, faith and hope!

notes.term: The Lord will give strength unto his people
notes.note: The last verse of a psalm about the Lord’s voice in a thunderstorm ([[Ps.29.11|Psalm 29:11]]).
Sends the lightning straight to its mark. Unerring means never missing.
“They shall mount up with wings as eagles” ([[Isa.40.31|Isaiah 40:31]]).
[[Isa.9.6|Isaiah 9:6]].
“For he is our peace” ([[Eph.2.14|Ephesians 2:14]]).
Rest.
Trouble, suffering.

modern: The highest service is imitation. If I want to be Christ’s servant, I must be his follower. Doing as Jesus did is the surest way to bring honor to his name. Let me remember this every day.

If I imitate Jesus, I’ll have his company: if I am like him, I’ll be with him. In due time he will take me up to live with him above, if in the meantime I have tried to follow him here below. After his suffering our Lord came to his throne, and in the same way, after we have suffered a while with him here below, we too will arrive in glory. The outcome of our Lord’s life will be the outcome of ours: if we are with him in his humiliation, we will be with him in his glory. Come, my soul, take courage, and set your feet in the blood-marked footprints your Lord has left you.

Let me not fail to notice that the Father will honor those who follow his Son. If he sees me true to Jesus, he will put marks of favor and honor on me for his Son’s sake. No honor can compare with this. Princes and emperors give only the shadows of honor; the substance of glory comes from the Father. So, my soul, cling to your Lord Jesus more closely than ever.

notes.term: If any man serve me, let him follow me

notes.note: Keep in mind; take care to do.

notes.term: After we have suffered a while with Him
notes.note: “If we suffer, we shall also reign with him” ([[2Tim.2.12|2 Timothy 2:12]]); “after that ye have suffered a while” ([[1Pet.5.10|1 Peter 5:10]]).
Outcome, result.
Being humbled, brought low; here, Christ’s humbling of himself “unto death, even the death of the cross” ([[Phil.2.8|Philippians 2:8]]).
Take courage.
So, therefore.

modern: Our unbelief is the greatest obstacle in our way; in fact, there is no other real difficulty in our spiritual progress and prosperity. The Lord can do everything; but when he makes a rule that it will be done to us according to our faith, our unbelief ties the hands of his omnipotence.

Yes, the alliances of evil will be scattered if only we can believe. Despised truth will lift its head if only we will trust the God of truth. We can carry our load of trouble, or pass unharmed through the waves of distress, if we can wrap our waist with the belt of peace, the belt that is buckled on by the hands of trust.

What can’t we believe? Is everything possible except believing in God? Yet he is always true; why don’t we believe him? He is always faithful to his word; why can’t we trust him? When our hearts are in a right state, faith takes no effort: it is then as natural for us to rely on God as for a child to trust its father.

The worst of it is that we can believe God about everything except the trial pressing on us right now. This is folly. Come, my soul, shake off such sinfulness, and trust your God with the load, the labor and the longing of this present moment. Do this, and all is done.

notes.note: Jesus to the father of the boy with an evil spirit ([[Mark.9.23-Mark.9.24|Mark 9:23–24]]).
“According to your faith be it unto you” ([[Matt.9.29|Matthew 9:29]]).
Being all-powerful.
Alliances, leagues.

notes.term: Gird our loins with the girdle
notes.note: Fasten a belt around our waist, as people did before work or a journey.

modern: The Lord Christ in the midst of his people is to be acknowledged and obeyed. He is God’s representative and speaks in the Father’s name, and it is for us to do what he commands, completely and at once. We’ll lose the promise if we disregard the command.

How large the blessing is for full obedience! The Lord enters into an alliance with his people, for attack and for defense. He will bless those who bless us, and curse those who curse us. God will go heart and soul with his people, and enter with the deepest sympathy into their situation. What protection this gives us! We needn’t worry about our enemies when we are sure they have become God’s enemies. If Jehovah has taken up our quarrel, we can leave the enemy in his hands.

As far as our own interests go, we have no enemies; but for the cause of truth and righteousness we take up arms and go out to the fight. In this holy war we are allied with the eternal God, and if we carefully obey the law of our Lord Jesus, he is committed to putting out all his power on our behalf. So we fear no one.

notes.term: I will be an enemy unto thine enemies
notes.note: Said of the Angel the Lord sent ahead of Israel: “Beware of him, and obey his voice… for my name is in him” ([[Exod.23.20-Exod.23.22|Exodus 23:20–22]]).
Someone who rules on behalf of another; a deputy.
Completely, without question.
A command.
An alliance for both attack and defense.

notes.term: Bless those who bless us, and curse those who curse us
notes.note: God’s promise to Abraham ([[Gen.12.3|Genesis 12:3]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Enemies.
Committed, pledged.
So, therefore.

modern: Trust and do are words that go well together, in the order the Holy Spirit has put them. We should have faith, and that faith should work. Trust in God sets us to holy doing: we trust God for good, and then we do good. We don’t sit still because we trust; we rouse ourselves and expect the Lord to work through us and by us. It isn’t ours to worry and do evil, but to trust and do good. We don’t trust without doing, or do without trusting.

Our enemies would root us out if they could; but by trusting and doing we live in the land. We won’t go down into Egypt, but we’ll stay in Immanuel’s land: the providence of God, the Canaan of covenant love. We aren’t as easy to get rid of as the Lord’s enemies think. They can’t push us out or stamp us out: where God has given us a name and a place, there we stay.

But what about the supply of our needs? The Lord has put a “verily” into this promise. As sure as God is true, his people will be fed. Their part is to trust and to do, and the Lord’s part is to do according to their trust. If they aren’t fed by ravens, or by an Obadiah, or by a widow, still they will be fed somehow. Away, you fears!

notes.term: Trust in the Lord, and do good
We will not go into Egypt
notes.note: God’s people were warned not to go down to Egypt for help ([[Isa.31.1|Isaiah 31:1]]).
The land of promise, which Isaiah calls “thy land, O Immanuel” ([[Isa.8.8|Isaiah 8:8]]); here, the place of God’s care.
God’s care and control over everything that happens, providing for his people.
Truly, surely.
Ravens brought Elijah bread and meat by the brook Cherith ([[1Kgs.17.6|1 Kings 17:6]]).
Obadiah hid a hundred of the Lord’s prophets in caves and fed them bread and water ([[1Kgs.18.4|1 Kings 18:4]]).
The widow of Zarephath fed Elijah, and her flour and oil never ran out ([[1Kgs.17.9-1Kgs.17.16|1 Kings 17:9–16]]).

modern: Fretting and worrying, questioning and mistrusting, are always weakness. What can we do if we wear ourselves to skin and bone? Can we gain anything by fearing and fuming? Don’t we unfit ourselves for action and unsettle our minds for wise decisions? We are sinking by our struggles when we could float by faith.

Oh, for grace to be quiet! Why run from house to house repeating the weary story that makes us more and more heartsick as we tell it? Why even stay at home and cry out in agony over miserable forebodings that may never come true? It would be good to keep a quiet tongue, but far better to have a quiet heart. Oh, to be still and know that Jehovah is God!

Oh, for grace to be confident in God! The Holy One of Israel must defend and rescue his own. He can’t go back on his solemn declarations. We can be sure that every word of his will stand, though the mountains should depart. He deserves to be trusted; and if we would show confidence, and the quietness that comes from it, we might be as happy as the spirits before the throne.
Come, my soul, return to your rest, and lean your head on the heart of the Lord Jesus.

notes.term: In quietness and in confidence shall be your strength
notes.note: [[Isa.30.15|Isaiah 30:15]]. Israel’s sad answer follows: “and ye would not.”
Feelings that something bad is coming.
“Be still, and know that I am God” ([[Ps.46.10|Psalm 46:10]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
“For the mountains shall depart… but my kindness shall not depart from thee” ([[Isa.54.10|Isaiah 54:10]]).
Trusted.
“Return unto thy rest, O my soul” ([[Ps.116.7|Psalm 116:7]]).
The chest, the place of closest embrace.

modern: It’s a surprise that it should be so, for everything threatens that at evening time it will be dark. God usually works in a way so far above our fears and beyond our hopes that we are greatly amazed, and led to praise his sovereign grace. No, it won’t be with us as our hearts are predicting: the dark won’t deepen into midnight, but will suddenly brighten into day. Let’s never despair. In the worst times let’s trust in the Lord, who turns the shadow of death into morning. When the count of bricks is doubled, Moses appears; and when trouble abounds, it is nearest its end.

This promise should help our patience. The light may not fully come until our hopes are quite worn out by waiting all day for nothing. For the wicked the sun goes down while it is still day; for the righteous the sun rises when it is almost night. Can’t we wait patiently for that heavenly light, which may be long in coming but is sure to prove well worth waiting for?
Come, my soul, take up your song, and sing to him who will bless you in life and in death, in a way that surpasses everything nature has ever seen at its best.

notes.term: At evening time it shall be light
notes.note: [[Zech.14.7|Zechariah 14:7]].
Used to; in the habit of.
God’s right and power to rule and to choose freely, answering to no one.

notes.term: Turneth the darkness of the shadow of death into the morning
notes.note: “Seek him that… turneth the shadow of death into the morning” ([[Amos.5.8|Amos 5:8]]).

notes.term: When the tale of bricks is doubled Moses appears
notes.note: A saying from the Exodus story. Pharaoh made the Israelites gather their own straw but still make the same tale, or count, of bricks; and then the Lord brought them out through Moses ([[Exod.5.6-Exod.5.8|Exodus 5:6–8]]). When things are at their worst, help is near.
Trouble, suffering.

notes.term: The sun goes down while it is yet day
notes.note: Of judgment: “her sun is gone down while it was yet day” ([[Jer.15.9|Jeremiah 15:9]]).
Speak out your song, as Balaam “took up his parable” ([[Num.23.7|Numbers 23:7]]).

modern: Glory be to his name! All things need to be made new, for they are badly battered and worn by sin. It’s time the old garment was rolled up and put away, and creation put on her Sunday best. But no one can make all things new except the Lord who made them in the first place, for it takes as much power to make something out of evil as to make it out of nothing. Our Lord Jesus has taken on the task, and he is fully able to do it. He has already begun his work, and for centuries he has kept on making new the hearts of men and the order of society. By and by he will make new the whole structure of human government, and human nature will be changed by his grace; and a day will come when the body will be made new and raised like his glorious body.

What a joy to belong to a kingdom in which everything is being made new by the power of its King! We aren’t dying out: we are hurrying on to a more glorious life. In spite of the opposition of the powers of evil, our glorious Lord Jesus is carrying out his purpose, and making us and everything around us “new,” and as full of beauty as when they first came from the hand of the Lord.

notes.term: Behold, I make all things new
notes.note: [[Rev.21.5|Revelation 21:5]].

notes.term: The old vesture was rolled up
notes.note: “As a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed” ([[Heb.1.12|Hebrews 1:12]]). A vesture is a garment.
The whole structure and order.
Before long; later on.

notes.term: Raised like unto His glorious body
notes.note: Christ “shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body” ([[Phil.3.21|Philippians 3:21]]).
Hurrying.

modern: Oh, if only these happy times had come! At present the nations are heavily armed, and keep inventing more and more terrible weapons, as if the chief end of man could only be served by destroying great numbers of his fellow men. Yet peace will win one day; yes, and win so completely that the instruments of destruction will be beaten into other shapes and used for better purposes.

How will this come about? By trade? By civilization? By arbitration? We don’t believe it. Past experience forbids us to trust such feeble means. Peace will be established only by the reign of the Prince of Peace. He must teach the people by his Spirit, renew their hearts by his grace and rule over them by his supreme power, and then they will stop wounding and killing. Man is a monster once his blood is up, and only the Lord Jesus can turn this lion into a lamb. By changing a man’s heart, he removes his bloodthirsty passions. Let every reader of this book of promises offer special prayer today to the Lord and Giver of peace, that he would quickly put an end to war and establish harmony over the whole world.

notes.term: They shall beat their swords into plowshares
notes.note: [[Isa.2.4|Isaiah 2:4]]. A plowshare is the blade of a plow; pruning hooks are curved knives for trimming vines.
An echo of the Westminster Shorter Catechism: “Man’s chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him for ever.”
Countless numbers.
Settling quarrels between nations through an agreed judge rather than by war.
[[Isa.9.6|Isaiah 9:6]].
Harmony, agreement.

modern: It’s a great encouragement to courage to be assured of victory, for then a man goes out to war with confidence, and goes where he would otherwise have been afraid to go. Our war is with evil within us and around us, and we ought to be convinced that we are able to win, and that we will win in the name of the Lord Jesus. We aren’t riding for a fall, but to win; and win we will. The grace of God in its omnipotence is put out to overthrow evil in every form: hence the certainty of triumph.

Some of our sins find chariots of iron in our temperament, our old habits, our companions and our jobs. Still, we must overcome them. They are very strong, and against them we are very weak; yet in the name of God we must master them, and we will. If one sin rules over us, we aren’t the Lord’s free men. A man held by only one chain is still a captive. There is no going to heaven with one sin ruling inside us, for of the saints it is said, “Sin shall not have dominion over you.” Up, then, and kill every Canaanite, and smash every chariot of iron to pieces! The Lord of hosts is with us, and who can resist his sin-destroying power?

notes.term: Thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots
notes.note: Joshua’s word to the tribes of Joseph, who complained that their land was too small and the Canaanites too strong ([[Josh.17.16-Josh.17.18|Joshua 17:16–18]]).
Courage.
Heading for disaster.
Being all-powerful.
Natural makeup; temperament.

notes.term: Sin shall not have dominion over you
notes.note: [[Rom.6.14|Romans 6:14]]. Dominion means rule.
Smash to pieces.

modern: While we are here, the Lord is with us; and when we are called away, we are with him. There is no dividing the saint from his Savior. They are one, and they must always be one: Jesus can’t be without his own people, for he would be a head without a body. Whether caught up into the air, or resting in paradise, or living here as strangers, we are with Jesus; and who will separate us from him?

What a joy this is! Our highest honor, rest, comfort and delight is to be with the Lord. We can’t imagine anything that could surpass or even equal this divine company. By holy fellowship we must be with him in his humiliation, rejection and toil, and then we will be with him in his glory. Before long we’ll be with him in his rest and in his royalty, in his waiting and in his revealing. We’ll fare as he fares, and triumph as he triumphs.

O my Lord, if I am to be with you forever, I have a destiny beyond compare. I won’t envy an archangel. To be forever with the Lord is my idea of heaven at its best. Not the harps of gold, nor the unfading crowns, nor the unclouded light is glory to me; but Jesus, Jesus himself, and myself forever with him in the nearest and dearest fellowship.

notes.term: So shall we ever be with the Lord
notes.note: Paul’s comfort about believers who have died and the Lord’s return ([[1Thess.4.16-1Thess.4.18|1 Thessalonians 4:16–18]]).
Living somewhere for a while as a stranger.

notes.term: Who shall separate us from Him?
notes.note: “Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?” ([[Rom.8.35|Romans 8:35]]).
Being humbled, brought low.
Hard labor, toil.
His waiting at God’s right hand “till his enemies be made his footstool” ([[Heb.10.12-Heb.10.13|Hebrews 10:12–13]]), and his appearing in glory.

modern: With hurrying wing the mother bird rushes to protect her young. She wastes no time on the way when she comes to bring them food or guard them from danger. So, as on eagles’ wings, the Lord will come to defend his chosen; yes, he will ride on the wings of the wind.

With outspread wing the mother covers her little ones in the nest. She hides them by putting her own body between them and harm. The hen gives her own warmth to her chicks, and makes her wings a house for them to live in. So Jehovah himself becomes the protection of his chosen. He himself is their refuge, their home, their all.

As birds flying and birds covering (for the word means both), so the Lord will be to us; and he will be this again and again, and successfully. We will be defended and kept from all evil. The Lord who compares himself to birds won’t be like them in their feebleness, for he is Jehovah of hosts. Let this be our comfort: almighty love will be swift to help and sure to cover. God’s wing is quicker and more tender than a bird’s wing, and from now on and forever we will put our trust under its shadow.

notes.term: As birds flying, so will the Lord of hosts defend Jerusalem

notes.note: “I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself” ([[Exod.19.4|Exodus 19:4]]).
“He did fly upon the wings of the wind” ([[Ps.18.10|Psalm 18:10]]).
Putting between.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
His chosen. The elect are God’s chosen people.
Help.
“In the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge” ([[Ps.57.1|Psalm 57:1]]).

modern: From the context, this promise belongs to the much-afflicted righteous man: “Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the Lord delivereth him out of them all.” He may suffer skin wounds and flesh wounds, but no great harm will be done: “not a bone of him shall be broken.”

This is a great comfort to a tested child of God, and a comfort I dare to accept; for up to this hour I have suffered no real damage from my many afflictions. I haven’t lost faith or hope or love. In fact, far from losing these bones of character, they have grown in strength and energy. I have more knowledge, more experience, more patience and more stability than I had before the trials came. Not even my joy has been destroyed. I’ve had many a bruise from sickness, bereavement, depression, slander and opposition; but the bruise has healed, and there has been no compound fracture of a bone, not even a simple one. The reason isn’t hard to find. If we trust in the Lord, he keeps all our bones; and if he keeps them, we can be sure that not one of them is broken.
Come, my heart, don’t grieve. You are smarting, but no bones are broken. Endure hardship, and defy fear.

notes.note: [[Ps.34.19-Ps.34.20|Psalm 34:19–20]]. Spurgeon’s “not a bone of him shall be broken” is John’s wording, for when the soldiers did not break Jesus’ legs ([[John.19.36|John 19:36]]).
The loss of a loved one by death.
A break where the bone pierces the skin; a simple fracture doesn’t.
Stinging with pain.
“Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ” ([[2Tim.2.3|2 Timothy 2:3]]).

modern: Let the text itself be taken as today’s portion. There’s no need to enlarge on it. Trembling one, read it, believe it, feed on it and plead it before the Lord. The one you fear is only a man after all, while the one who promises to comfort you is God, your Maker, the Creator of heaven and earth. Infinite comfort more than covers a very limited danger.

“Where is the fury of the oppressor?” It is in the Lord’s hand. It is only the fury of a dying creature, fury that will end as soon as the breath has left his nostrils. Why, then, should we stand in awe of someone as frail as ourselves? Let’s not dishonor our God by making a god of puny man. We can make an idol of a man by giving him too much fear as well as by giving him too much love. Let’s treat men as men and God as God; and then we will go calmly on in the path of duty, fearing the Lord and fearing nobody else.

notes.term: I, even I, am he that comforteth you

notes.note: A share of an inheritance. Here, today’s share of God’s word to feed on.

notes.term: The breath is gone from the nostril
notes.note: “Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils” ([[Isa.2.22|Isaiah 2:22]]).
Excessive.

modern: God never turns from his love, but he soon turns from his anger. His love for his chosen comes from his nature; his anger comes only from his office. He loves because he is love; he frowns because it is necessary for our good. He will come back to the place where his heart rests, namely his love for his own, and then he will take pity on our griefs and end them.

What a choice promise this is: “He will subdue our iniquities”! He will conquer them. They try to enslave us, but the Lord will give us victory over them by his own right hand. Like the Canaanites, they will be beaten, put under the yoke and finally killed.

As for the guilt of our sins, how gloriously it is removed! “All their sins”: yes, the whole army of them. “Thou wilt cast”: only an almighty arm could do such a wonder. “Into the depths of the sea”: where Pharaoh and his chariots went down. Not into the shallows, where the tide might wash them up again, but into the “depths” our sins will be hurled. They are all gone. They sank to the bottom like a stone. Hallelujah! Hallelujah!

notes.term: He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us
notes.note: “Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity… he delighteth in mercy” ([[Mic.7.18-Mic.7.19|Micah 7:18–19]]).
His role; here, as the Judge and Father who must correct.
“God is love” ([[1John.4.8|1 John 4:8]]).
Conquer our sins. Iniquities are wickednesses.
Surely a misprint in this edition for “They try to enslave us.”
Made to serve, like a conquered people.

notes.term: Where Pharaoh and his chariots went down
notes.note: “The depths have covered them: they sank into the bottom as a stone” ([[Exod.15.5|Exodus 15:5]]).

modern: A help that isn’t there when we need it is of little value. The anchor left at home is no use to the sailor in the hour of storm; the money he used to have is worth nothing to the debtor when a writ is out against him. Very few earthly helps could be called “very present”: they are usually far off when we look for them, far off when we try to use them, and farther still once they have been used. But as for the Lord our God, he is present when we seek him, present when we need him, and present when we have already enjoyed his help.

He is more than “present”; he is very present. More present than the nearest friend can be, for he is in us in our trouble; more present than we are to ourselves, for sometimes we lack presence of mind. He is always present, effectually present, sympathetically present, altogether present. He is present now, if this is a gloomy time. Let’s rest on him. He is our refuge: let’s hide in him. He is our strength: let’s clothe ourselves with him. He is our help: let’s lean on him. He is our very present help: let’s rest in him now. We needn’t have a moment’s worry or an instant’s fear. “The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge.”

notes.term: A very present help in trouble
A writ is out against him
notes.note: A court order has been issued for his arrest or for seizing his goods.
Effective; actually doing what it sets out to do. Here, present to real effect.
The ability to stay calm and think clearly in a crisis.

notes.term: The Lord of hosts is with us

modern: We may be rich in things like those Joseph received, and we may have them in a higher sense. Oh, for “the precious things of heaven”! Power with God, and the showing of power from God, are most precious. We want to enjoy the peace of God, the joy of the Lord, the glory of our God. The blessing of the three divine Persons, in love and grace and fellowship, we value above the finest gold. The things of earth are nothing in preciousness compared with the things of heaven.

“The dew.” How precious this is! How we pray and praise when we have the dew! What refreshing, what growth, what fragrance, what life there is in us when the dew is about! Above all else, as plants of the Lord’s own right-hand planting, we need the dew of his Holy Spirit.

“The deep that coucheth beneath.” Surely this refers to the unseen ocean underground that supplies all the fresh springs that gladden the earth. Oh, to tap the eternal fountains! This is a gift beyond words; let no believer rest until he has it. The all-sufficiency of Jehovah is ours forever. Let’s turn to it now.

notes.note: From Moses’ last blessing on the tribes ([[Deut.33.13|Deuteronomy 33:13]]).
Showing.
A blessing. Here, the blessing of Father, Son and Holy Spirit: “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost” ([[2Cor.13.14|2 Corinthians 13:14]]).
Life-giving moisture in a dry land; a picture of God’s blessing. “I will be as the dew unto Israel” ([[Hos.14.5|Hosea 14:5]]).

notes.term: Plants of the Lord’s own right hand planting
notes.note: Those God himself has planted ([[Ps.80.15|Psalm 80:15]]).
Lies crouching; lies hidden.
A gift, a blessing.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

modern: That archenemy the devil has been a liar from the beginning; but he is so very plausible that, like mother Eve, we are led to believe him. Yet in our experience we will prove him a liar.

He says we will fall from grace, dishonor our profession and perish with the doom of those who abandon the faith; but, trusting in the Lord Jesus, we will hold on our way and prove that Jesus loses none of those his Father gave him. He tells us that our bread will run out and we will starve with our children; yet the Feeder of the ravens hasn’t forgotten us yet, and he never will, but will prepare a table for us in the presence of our enemies.

He whispers that the Lord won’t rescue us out of the trial looming in the distance, and threatens that the last ounce will break the camel’s back. What a liar he is! For the Lord will never leave us or forsake us. “Let him deliver him now!” cries the false fiend; but the Lord will silence him by coming to our rescue.

He takes great delight in telling us that death will be too much for us. “How wilt thou do in the swelling of Jordan?” But there too he will prove a liar to us, and we will pass through the river singing psalms of glory.

notes.term: Thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee
notes.note: The last verse of Moses’ blessing on Israel ([[Deut.33.29|Deuteronomy 33:29]]).
“He was a murderer from the beginning… for he is a liar, and the father of it” ([[John.8.44|John 8:44]]).
Publicly claiming to be a Christian. A “dead profession” is the claim with no faith behind it.
Those who abandon the faith.

notes.term: Jesus loses none whom His Father gave Him
notes.note: “Of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing” ([[John.6.39|John 6:39]]).
“He giveth to the beast his food, and to the young ravens which cry” ([[Ps.147.9|Psalm 147:9]]).

notes.term: Prepare us a table in the presence of our enemies

notes.note: What the mockers said at the cross ([[Matt.27.43|Matthew 27:43]]).

notes.term: How wilt thou do in the swelling of Jordan?
notes.note: [[Jer.12.5|Jeremiah 12:5]]. The Jordan in flood stands for death.

modern: Many are celebrating our Lord’s first coming today; let’s turn our thoughts to the promise of his second coming. It is as sure as the first, and draws much of its certainty from it. He who came as a lowly man to serve will certainly come to take the reward of his service. He who came to suffer won’t be slow to come and reign.

This is our glorious hope, for we will share his joy. Today we are hidden and humbled, as he was while he was here below; but when he comes, it will be our unveiling, just as it will be his revealing. Dead saints will live at his appearing. The slandered and despised will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Then the saints will appear as kings and priests, and the days of their mourning will be over. The long rest and unimaginable splendor of the millennial reign will be a rich reward for the ages of witnessing and warring.
Oh, that the Lord would come! He is coming! He is on the road and traveling quickly. The sound of his approach should be music to our hearts! Ring out, you bells of hope!

notes.term: This same Jesus… shall so come in like manner
notes.note: The angels’ words as Jesus was taken up into heaven ([[Acts.1.9-Acts.1.11|Acts 1:9–11]]).
A coming or arrival. The Second Advent is Christ’s return.
Our being shown for who we are… his being revealed. “When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory” ([[Col.3.4|Colossians 3:4]]).
“Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father” ([[Matt.13.43|Matthew 13:43]]).
[[Rev.1.6|Revelation 1:6]].

notes.term: The days of their mourning shall be ended

notes.note: The thousand-year reign of Christ ([[Rev.20.4|Revelation 20:4]]).
Reward.

modern: “Why,” cries someone, “this is no promise of God.” Just so; but it was a promise of man, and so it came to nothing. Peter thought he was saying what he would certainly carry out; but a promise with no better foundation than a human resolution will fall to the ground. As soon as temptations arose, Peter denied his Master and swore oaths to back up his denial.

What is a human word? A clay pot broken at one blow. What is your own resolution? A blossom that, with God’s care, may come to fruit, but left to itself will fall to the ground with the first wind that moves the branch.
On a human word, hang only what it will bear.
On your own resolution, depend not at all.
On the promise of your God, hang time and eternity, this world and the next, your all and the all of all your loved ones.

This book is a checkbook for believers, and this page is meant as a warning about which bank they draw on and whose signature they accept. Rely on Jesus without limit. Don’t trust yourself or anyone born of woman beyond proper bounds; but trust only and wholly in the Lord.

notes.term: Though all men shall be offended because of thee
notes.note: Peter’s boast on the night of Jesus’ arrest ([[Matt.26.33-Matt.26.35|Matthew 26:33–35]]). To be offended here is to stumble and fall away.

notes.term: Used oaths to confirm his denial
notes.note: “Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man” ([[Matt.26.74|Matthew 26:74]]).

notes.term: An earthen pot broken with a stroke
notes.note: “He shall break it as the breaking of the potters’ vessel” ([[Isa.30.14|Isaiah 30:14]]).
Spurgeon’s title: each promise is like a check drawn on God’s bank, to be signed in faith and presented.

modern: One of the most delightful qualities of God’s love is that it lasts. The pillars of the earth may be moved out of their places, but the kindness and the covenant of our merciful Jehovah never leave his people. How happy my soul feels in firmly believing this inspired declaration! The year is almost over, and the years of my life are growing few, but time doesn’t change my Lord. New lamps are taking the place of the old; constant change is on all things; but our Lord is the same. Force overturns the hills, but no power imaginable can affect the eternal God. Nothing in the past, the present or the future can make Jehovah unkind to me.

My soul, rest in the eternal kindness of the Lord, who treats you as a close relative. Remember also the everlasting covenant. God always keeps it in mind; see that you keep it in mind too. In Christ Jesus the glorious God has pledged himself to you to be your God, and to hold you as one of his people. Kindness and covenant: dwell on these words as sure and lasting things that eternity itself won’t take from you.

notes.note: The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
God “shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble” ([[Job.9.6|Job 9:6]]).
A close relative; compare Boaz, Ruth’s kinsman-redeemer: “The man is near of kin unto us” ([[Ruth.2.20|Ruth 2:20]]).

modern: Several times in Scripture the Lord has said this. He has often repeated it, to make our assurance doubly sure. Let’s never entertain a doubt about it. In itself the promise is especially emphatic. In the Greek it has five negatives, each one firmly shutting out any possibility that the Lord will ever leave one of his people so that he could rightly feel forsaken by his God. This priceless scripture doesn’t promise us freedom from trouble, but it does guarantee us against desertion. We may be called to travel strange roads, but we’ll always have our Lord’s company, help and provision. We needn’t covet money, for we will always have our God, and God is better than gold; his favor is better than fortune.
We surely ought to be content with what we have, for whoever has God has more than all the world besides. What more can we have than the Infinite? What more can we want than Almighty Goodness?
Come, my heart: if God says he will never leave you or forsake you, pray much for grace, so that you may never leave your Lord, nor forsake his ways even for a moment.

notes.term: I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee
notes.note: “Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee” ([[Heb.13.5|Hebrews 13:5]]).
To Jacob ([[Gen.28.15|Genesis 28:15]]), to Israel and to Joshua ([[Deut.31.6|Deuteronomy 31:6]]; [[Josh.1.5|Joshua 1:5]]), and through David to Solomon ([[1Chr.28.20|1 Chronicles 28:20]]).
The Greek piles up “not” and “never”, as if to say, “I will never, never, no never leave you.”
Being let off; freedom from.
Long greedily for.

modern: The year is very old, and here is a promise for our aged friends; yes, and for us all, as age creeps over us. If we live long enough, we’ll all have gray hair; so we might as well enjoy this promise ahead of time by the foresight of faith.

When we grow old, our God will still be the I AM, always the same. Gray hairs tell of our decay, but he doesn’t decay. When we can’t carry a burden and can hardly carry ourselves, the Lord will carry us. Just as in our young days he carried us like lambs in his arms, so he will in our years of weakness.

He made us, and he will care for us. When we become a burden to our friends and a burden to ourselves, the Lord won’t shake us off; rather, he will take us up and carry us and rescue us more fully than ever. In many cases the Lord gives his servants a long, calm evening. They worked hard all day and wore themselves out in their Master’s service, and so he said to them, “Now rest in anticipation of that eternal Sabbath which I have prepared for you.” Let’s not dread old age. Let’s grow old graciously, since the Lord himself is with us in fullness of grace.

notes.term: Even to hoar hairs will I carry you
notes.note: [[Isa.46.4|Isaiah 46:4]]. Hoar hairs are gray or white hair.
God’s name revealed to Moses ([[Exod.3.14|Exodus 3:14]]).
“He shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom” ([[Isa.40.11|Isaiah 40:11]]).
Weaknesses; here, the weakness of old age.
Rather; instead.
“There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God” ([[Heb.4.9|Hebrews 4:9]]).

modern: This fact is really a promise; for what our Lord was, he is, and what he was to those he lived with on earth, he will be to all his loved ones as long as the moon endures.
“Having loved”: here was the wonder! That he should ever have loved people at all is the marvel. What was there in his poor disciples that he should love them? What is there in me?

But once he has begun to love, it is his nature to go on. Love made the saints “his own”: what a choice title! He bought them with blood, and they became his treasure. Since they are his own, he won’t lose them. Since they are his beloved, he won’t stop loving them. My soul, he won’t stop loving you!

The text is good just as it stands: “to the end.” Right up to his death, the ruling passion of love for his own reigned in his sacred heart. It also means to the uttermost. He couldn’t love them more: he gave himself for them. Some translate it “to perfection.” Truly he lavished on them a perfect love, in which there was no flaw or failure, no foolishness, no unfaithfulness and no holding back.
Such is the love of Jesus for each one of his people. Let’s sing a song to our Beloved.

notes.note: The opening of the Last Supper in John’s Gospel ([[John.13.1|John 13:1]]).

notes.term: So long as the moon endureth
notes.note: “As long as the moon endureth” ([[Ps.72.7|Psalm 72:7]]).
“The church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood” ([[Acts.20.28|Acts 20:28]]).
The chest, the place of closest embrace.
The Greek words for “unto the end” can also mean “completely” or “to the utmost”.
A name for Christ, from the Song of Solomon’s “my wellbeloved” ([[Song.1.13|Song of Solomon 1:13]]).

modern: From day to day and from year to year my faith trusts in the wisdom and love of God, and I know I won’t believe in vain. No good word of his has ever failed, and I am sure none ever will fall to the ground.

I put myself into his hand for guidance. I don’t know which way to choose: the Lord will choose my inheritance for me. I need counsel and advice, for my duties are complicated and my situation is tangled. I seek the Lord, as the high priest of old looked to his Urim and Thummim. I seek the counsel of the God who is never wrong in preference to my own judgment or the advice of friends. Glorious Jehovah, you will guide me!

Soon the end will come: a few more years, and I must leave this world and go to the Father. My Lord will be near my bed. He will meet me at heaven’s gate; he will welcome me to the land of glory. I won’t be a stranger in heaven: my own God and Father will receive me into its endless bliss.
GLORY BE TO HIM WHO
WILL GUIDE ME HERE,
AND RECEIVE ME HEREAFTER. AMEN.

notes.term: Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel

notes.note: Go unfulfilled. “There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken” ([[Josh.21.45|Joshua 21:45]]).

notes.term: The Lord shall choose mine inheritance for me
notes.note: “He shall choose our inheritance for us” ([[Ps.47.4|Psalm 47:4]]).
Complicated, tangled.
Objects kept in the high priest’s breastplate and used to ask God’s will ([[Exod.28.30|Exodus 28:30]]).
Never wrong.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

notes.term: Depart out of this world unto the Father
notes.note: Jesus’ own going home is described the same way ([[John.13.1|John 13:1]]).
In the life to come.
